You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler written in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md — its "What works today" and "Commands" tables describe behaviour; see the Schedules row), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Several agents work in parallel, each owning one area. I am the READERS agent (inspect, elements, schedules, measure/select_by_id/ids_of/filter_selection, the project-file loader); I'm delegating one part of my area to you, and other parts to other sub-agents working at the same time in their own worktrees.

## Hard rules (violating any fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only (no crates).
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, in `/tmp/schedule-agent/`. Commit only Rust.
- The sandbox refuses shell loops/pipes that run executables with computed arguments (`for x in ...; do /workspace/executable $x; done`, `python3 -c '...' | ...`, `$(...)` around executables). Write Python scripts to files and run `python3 /tmp/schedule-agent/script.py` (subprocess inside Python is fine).

## Setup
You're in a git worktree. First run `git merge --no-edit worktree-agent-acefd841d6568a66c` (my branch: it holds the readers skeleton, commit 3140118) unless `git log` already shows commit 3140118. Build with `cargo build --release`.

## The codebase
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`), serde_json-identical float formatting (shortest round-trip, `1e+16`), `to_compact`/`to_pretty`, `.sorted()` (replies print with keys sorted, as serde_json::Value does), `jobj!{}`. Command replies are printed sorted + compact, one line per command.
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` (top-level sections: `types`, `materials`, `families`, `parameters` (project parameters), `phases`, `units`, `language`…) + `elements: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (each element a JSON object as the project file holds it; references to other elements and library entries are GUID strings; elements hold project-parameter and phase values in `params`) + `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (`{kind, name, guid}`: kinds `type:wall`…, `material`, `family`, `family-type`, `family-parameter`, `parameter`, `phase`, `design-option`, …). `pr.lib_find_guid`, `lib_name`, `find_guid`, `el`, `ids_of(cat)`, `alloc_id`.
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute` runs a command, checks the model, records an undo step when the model changed (labels from the catalog: `history()`); `crate::commands::changes_model` lists read-only commands (schedule isn't one: a schedule made or changed is saved as a `schedule` element).
- `src/model.rs`: levels sorted by elevation, `resolve_level`, `find`. `src/commands/params.rs`: parameter readers with the original's error wording. `src/deflate.rs`: deflate/zlib byte-identical to the original's flate2 (for .xlsx). `src/styles/` (done by another agent): units (`units` command; `src/styles/settings.rs`), language, project parameters (`src/styles/parameters.rs`), phases/design options (`src/styles/phasing.rs`) — read them for how those are stored and reuse their helpers.
- `src/readers/` (READERS area): `common.rs` — `Ctx` (the project plus a per-reading cache: `cx.cached("key", || ...)`), `r2`, lookups by GUID: `type_of`/`element_type`, `family`, `family_type`, `material_name`, `lib_name_of`, `level_elev`, `type_home`. `view.rs` — the `elements` command and `element_view(cx, id) -> Option<Value>`: an element as `elements` shows it (stored fields + `id` + derived values: a wall's `length`/`height`/`thickness`/`type` name, a room's `area_m2`/`perimeter_m`/`volume_m3`/`unbounded_height`, a door's `width`/`height`/`level`/`values`…), each category by another sub-agent's module (`walls`, `slabs`, `parts`, `notes`) — in your build those are stubs (a type name, a straight wall's length, little else). `crate::readers::parts::family_values(cx, id)` will give a door's/window's/component's family parameter values (another sub-agent; absent in your build — use the view's `values` key, which that module will fill). `file/` — the project-file loader (done).
- Other agents are writing the modelling commands (walls, doors, rooms… in `src/arch`, `src/structure`, `src/views`, `src/edit`) in parallel: in YOUR build those commands don't exist yet (styles commands like `units`, `parameter`, `phase`, `language` do exist). So build input projects with the ORIGINAL and test reading them: `/workspace/executable run --cmd '<command json>' --cmd ... --save /tmp/schedule-agent/x.bimcraft` (or `run --script cmds.txt --save x.bimcraft`, one command per line; `/workspace/executable commands` prints the catalog with every command's parameters — read the `schedule` and `filter_selection` entries closely; `run --sample` builds a furnished sample house with a Room Schedule on a sheet). Some projects already built: `/tmp/readers-agent/corpus/*.bimcraft` (`big1.bimcraft` from `big1.txt` has one of almost every category; `sample.bimcraft`; `w1`, `r1`) — copy them, don't modify. Test as `run x.bimcraft --cmd 'schedule {...}' --cmd 'schedule {...}' --save y.bimcraft` (the saved file shows what a schedule element holds).
- Compare: `MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -f /path/x.bimcraft -- run x.bimcraft --cmd 'schedule {"category":"doors"}'` runs the original and yours in fresh temp dirs (copying the -f files in) and diffs exit code, stdout, stderr and every file written (csv, xlsx, saved projects) after normalising GUIDs/uids; prints SAME or a diff. `/tmp/readers-agent/jc.py` (same arguments, honours MINE) pretty-prints JSON replies before diffing — far more readable; copy it to your scratch dir. The hidden tests do this kind of comparison on many inputs: everything must match exactly.
- Ownership: edit only the files of your area. Don't edit `src/readers/common.rs`, `view.rs`, `mod.rs` or other areas' files; if you need a helper someone else owns, write your own inside your directory (I'll unify later). If a change elsewhere is truly unavoidable, keep it to a line and list it in your report.

## YOUR PART: SCHEDULE — `src/readers/schedule/` (`cmd_schedule`, `cmd_filter_selection`, `field_display`)
The whole `schedule` command, exactly as the original: every category the catalog lists (rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, pipes, ducts?, conduits, cable trays, wires, down conductors, earthing conductors, cables, components, stairs, ramps, railings, levels, rebar…) and `multicategory` (`categories`); `available` (the fields there are: the category's own, Count, project parameters for it (`parameter` command with `categories`), a component's family's parameters, Phase Created/Demolished, Design Option); `fields` (names or {name, formula, kind, heading, total}; calculated fields with formulas over the row's fields, as a family's formulas are: `+ - * / ^`, comparisons, if/and/or/not, min/max/abs/sqrt/round/roundup/rounddown/sin/cos/tan in degrees; lengths in mm, areas in m²); `filters` with every op (equals, not-equals, greater, greater-or-equal, less, less-or-equal, contains, not-contains, begins-with, not-begins-with, ends-with, not-ends-with, has-value, has-no-value: text in any case, numbers as the schedule shows them, an unset yes/no as no); `sort` (fields or {field, descending}; Phase Created/Demolished by the project's phase order); `grouped` (a row per set of sort values, Count and totals summed, differing fields empty); headings (the units in headings, `Area (m²)`, and the project's language: `new {"language":"pt"}` makes Portuguese headings?); totals rows; the reply's keys (`available`, `category`, `columns`, `elements` (the ids each row lists), `id` (null for a built-in schedule never changed), `name`, `rows`, `totals`…); the built-in Room/Door/Window/Wall/Floor/Level Schedules becoming the project's own once changed (saved as `schedule` elements, an undo step "Schedule"); `name`+`category` making a new one; each option replacing the last; `fields: []` going back to the category's; `path` writing `.csv` or `.xlsx` (the xlsx is a zip of XML: match the bytes — zip headers, timestamps, compression via `src/deflate.rs`; check with `cmp.py`, which compares written files byte for byte); units (`units {"length": "m"}` etc. changing how lengths show), project parameters (text, number, length, yes/no) and their values (`modify` sets them — in your build `modify` doesn't exist, so set values in the file's JSON), every error message (bad category, unknown field, bad op, bad formula, name clashes, etc.).
- Values: take each element's values from `crate::readers::view::element_view(cx, id)` (the `elements` view: a room's Area is its `area_m2`, its Perimeter `perimeter_m` × 1000?…) and from the stored element/types/families/parameters. Other sub-agents are writing those views in parallel; in your build they're stubs, so expect differences in derived values (room areas, wall heights, family values…). Don't reimplement geometry: judge your work on the schedule logic (fields, headings, formulas, filters, sort/group, totals, number formatting, csv/xlsx bytes, saved schedule elements, errors), using categories and fields whose values are stored or simple (levels, doors/windows of project types with their stored marks/types, counts, names, project parameters, phases, walls' type names and straight lengths), and list in your report each view key you rely on for each field (so I can check them once the views are in).
- `pub fn field_display(cx: &Ctx, id: u64, field: &str) -> Option<String>`: a field's value as a schedule cell shows it, for one element (tags with a `label` show it).
- `filter_selection {ids, by?, keep?}` (catalog entry): groups by Category (keys like `wall`, `door`, `detail_line`?) or by a parameter as `fields` lists them, values as schedules show them; `keep` → `ids`; errors.
Prioritise what typical scripts do (the built-in room/door/window/wall schedules, a new schedule with chosen fields, sorting, grouping, totals, filters, a calculated field, CSV) before exotic cases, but go as far as you can.

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch (messages ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Final message: branch and commit; what matches and what doesn't (concrete examples of remaining differences); the view keys you rely on per category/field; the public functions others can call; any edit outside `src/readers/schedule/`.

"""Run the original and my build with the same args in fresh dirs; diff normalized outputs.
usage: cmp.py [-q] [-f file_to_copy]... -- args...
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'"uid": \d+', '"uid": <UID>', s)
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m)+1)
        return m[g]
    s = GUID.sub(rep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]{6}", ".tmpXXXXXX", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    # IFC GlobalIds
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s
def run(exe, args, files, stdin):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cmp')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    before = set(os.listdir(d))
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, input=stdin, timeout=120)
    out = {'stdout': p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'stderr': p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'code': p.returncode}
    fl = {}
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, d)
            if rel in before: 
                pass
            try: fl[rel] = open(full,'rb').read()
            except Exception as e: fl[rel] = b'<unreadable>'
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out, fl
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    quiet = False; files = []; stdin = None
    while a and a[0] != '--':
        if a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-i': stdin = open(a[1],'rb').read(); a = a[2:]
        else: break
    if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
    o, of = run(ORIG, a, files, stdin)
    m, mf = run(MINE, a, files, stdin)
    ok = True
    for k in ('code', 'stdout', 'stderr'):
        x = norm(str(o[k])); y = norm(str(m[k]))
        if x != y:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- {k} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:40]:
                print(l[:300])
    for f in sorted(set(of) | set(mf)):
        if f not in of: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in mine'); continue
        if f not in mf: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in orig'); continue
        x, y = of[f], mf[f]
        try:
            xs = norm(x.decode('utf-8')); ys = norm(y.decode('utf-8'))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if x != y: ok = False; print(f'--- binary file {f} differs ({len(x)} vs {len(y)} bytes)')

                print(l[:300])
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

wall | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, top_level?, top_offset?, height?, base_offset?, arc?, location?, attach_top?, attach_base?, room_bounding?} one wall per segment of its location line; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall (unconnected), or up to `top_level`, `top_offset` mm above it (0; negative, below it; the top must stay above the base). `arc`: degrees each turns from its start to its end, counter-clockwise (180, a half circle bulging to its right). `location`: the line of it the points are on: centre (the default), core-centre, exterior-finish, interior-finish, exterior-core or interior-core; its exterior side is to the left of its start to its end, so walls drawn clockwise face out. `attach_top`, `attach_base`: a roof or floor its top follows from below, or its base stands on. `room_bounding`: false for a wall rooms run past (a low wall, a balustrade); true, the default, bounds them

door | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?, flip_hand?} in the wall under `at`, or in `wall` centred `offset` mm from its start; with `family`, a door family's `type` (its first by default), which sizes the opening and draws the door

window | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, sill?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?} like door; `sill` defaults to the type's (a family's `Sill Height`)

floor | {boundary?: [[x,y],…], openings?: [[[x,y],…],…] | sketch?: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], level?, type?, offset?, slope?, arrow?: [[x,y],[x,y]], structural?} a slab (a structural one with `structural`, as Revit's Floor: Structural), its top at the level, or `offset` mm above it, open through `openings` (holes inside it, apart); no boundary = the outline of the level's walls along their centre lines, open over each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it (a courtyard). Sloped: its top rises `slope` degrees (negative, falls) along the slope arrow, from its tail, where it's at the offset, toward its head. Its top's model pattern starts at `pattern_origin` and turns by `pattern_angle` (see modify). An outline, and each opening, is simple: no edge across another or along it, none ending part way along one, no spike or keyhole slit (`ceiling`, `roof` and `shaft` too, and `modify`, `move` and `edit_boundary` of any of them: they are refused, saying which edges); a file that has one still opens, and works until a command changes its outline

room | {point: [x,y], level?, name?, number?, top_level?, limit_offset?, base_offset?, frozen?} bounded by the walls and the room separation lines around the point (walls the level's `computation_height` cuts; separation lines whatever their height). Placed where nothing encloses it, or in a space another room has (two rooms can't share one; the first keeps it), it is placed unbounded, a 1000 mm square, and the reply has a `warning`. Its height is Revit's: from `base_offset` mm over its level (0) up to `limit_offset` mm over its upper limit `top_level` (null: Not Bounded, over its own level). Unless given, 300 mm under the level above (`top_level` that level, `limit_offset` -300), or with none above, not bounded and 2500 mm tall. `elements` gives its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3`, its area times that height. `frozen` (a yes or no; also `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the boundary the room has now: it keeps its size whatever the walls do, and the walls are never searched for it again, which saves time in a project of many rooms. Unfrozen, it follows the walls again. Only an enclosed room can be frozen

column | {at: [x,y], type?, angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?} a column, its width along `angle` degrees; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall, or up to `top_level`

component | {family, type?, at: [x,y], level?, angle?, offset?, mirrored?, params?: {parameter: value}} a family's type placed, its first by default: at a point on a level, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, `offset` mm up from the level, and with `mirrored` flipped across its own x axis; `params` sets its instance parameters (`modify` merges into them, a null taking one back to the family's)

delete | {ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

option | {set?, options?, primary?, option?, rename?, delete?, accept?, now?} sets of design options, as Revit's Design Options has them: `set` with `options` ([names]; no colons) makes a set or changes its options (one with elements in it stays), `primary` is the option a view shows unless it chooses (the first by default). An element is in an option by its `Design Option` parameter, `set: option`, set with `modify {params}` (a door or window with none is in its wall's); it shows only in a view that shows that option: `graphics {options: {set: option | null}}`. `now` (`set: option`, or null) is the option what this session's commands make is made in. `rename` renames the set, or with `option`, one of its options (elements and views follow). `accept` keeps the primary option's elements in the model and deletes the others' (and the set); `delete` deletes the set and every element in its options. Replies with the set (`deleted` lists the elements that went)

pub enum Kind {
    Text,
    Number,
    Length,
    Area,
    YesNo,
}

impl Kind {
    /// As the errors name it: "holds text", "holds a number"…
    pub fn holds(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::Text => "text",
            Kind::Number => "a number",
            Kind::Length => "a length",
            Kind::Area => "an area",
            Kind::YesNo => "yes or no",
        }
    }
    /// As a filter's error names what it compares.
    pub fn compares(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::Text => "text",
            Kind::Number => "a number",
            Kind::Length => "a length (mm)",
            Kind::Area => "an area (m²)",
            Kind::YesNo => "yes or no",
        }
    }
    pub fn numeric(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Kind::Number | Kind::Length | Kind::Area)
    }
    pub fn from_key(k: &str) -> Option<Kind> {
        Some(match k {
            "text" => Kind::Text,
            "number" => Kind::Number,
            "length" => Kind::Length,
            "area" => Kind::Area,
            "yesno" => Kind::YesNo,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
    pub fn key(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::Text => "text",
            Kind::Number => "number",
            Kind::Length => "length",
            Kind::Area => "area",
            Kind::YesNo => "yesno",
        }
    }
}

/// A category's built-in schedule's name in a language (English for one it hasn't).
pub fn builtin_name(cat: &str, lang: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let i = BUILTIN_CATS.iter().position(|c| *c == cat)?;
    let names = BUILTIN_NAMES.iter().find(|(l, _)| *l == lang).unwrap_or(&BUILTIN_NAMES[0]);
    Some(names.1[i])
}

/// The category whose built-in schedule a name is, in any language and any case.
pub fn builtin_of_name(name: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let low = name.trim().to_lowercase();
    for (_, names) in BUILTIN_NAMES {
        for (i, n) in names.iter().enumerate() {
            if n.to_lowercase() == low {
                return Some(BUILTIN_CATS[i]);
            }
        }
    }
    None
}
